To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the teachers in our study had different conceptions of the attitudes that problems can produce in the students and they also had different ideas of the reasons why problems can generate positive or negative attitudes.

(a) teachers' conceptions of mathematics problems in secondary textbooks are influenced by a variety of factors, such as the nature of the problems themselves, teachers' personal experience and knowledge of mathematics, and teachers' beliefs about the nature and role of mathematics; and (b) teachers' connotations of the problems are related to the way in which they think about the nature and the teaching and learning of mathematics.
teachers' perceptions of the problems presented in textbooks are related to the context in which the problems are presented and that teachers' perceptions are related to their teaching style.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the study of the conceptions of teachers about the problems proposed in the textbooks of mathematics in secondary education, in terms of the positive or negative attitudes they can generate among students.
the analysis of the attitudes that students have towards mathematical problems, and the way these problems are presented in mathematics textbooks.
the attitudes that problems and exercises proposed in textbooks can generate among pupils in secondary school.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
(1) the teachers have a positive attitude toward the problems in their books, and (2) they consider that the problems are the main factor in the development of positive attitudes toward mathematics.

1) the problems in the textbooks generate positive attitudes when they are related to situations that are meaningful for the students, 2) the problems in which the students have to use their own knowledge and experience generate positive attitudes, 3) the problems in mathematics that have a practical application in the students’ daily lives also generate positive attitudes, and 4) the problems that have a mathematical content, but are not related to the daily life of the students generate negative attitudes.
the problems and exercises proposed in textbooks generate attitudes towards mathematics in students that are positive or negative depending on the contexts in which they are immersed.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have found a set of problems and exercises that are considered to be positive by the teachers, and a set of problems that are considered negative by them.

we have found that the teachers are aware of the fact that problems can be presented with different degrees of complexity, and that they can be presented in different contexts, but they do not seem to have a clear idea of how to use the problems to generate positive or negative attitudes towards mathematics.

we have analyzed some works about this problem, in the sense of that problems proposed in mathematics textbooks generate liking or dislike of mathematics, depending on the contexts in which they are immersed.

the teachers' conceptions about the attitudes that the problems and exercises proposed in the mathematics textbooks in secondary education generate in students, are based on the contexts in which these problems are immersed.
